newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Diffs finish mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Diffs finish mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Conventional gasoline differentials on the U.S. Gulf Coast firmed Friday, while Chicago low sulphur diesel weakened in very quiet market activity.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained 1.31 cents and August gasoline gained 1.25 cents, while July heating oil surged 1.12 cents and August heating oil jumped 1.13 cent.
Regular unleaded gasoline differentials firmed in a slow Friday session following Thursday's volatile moves on the prompt cycle's scheduling deadling on the Colonial Pipeline.
"We did so much trading in the last few days that a lot of people just quit to get an early start on the weekend,' said a U.S. Gulf Coast trader.

USG M1 prompt cycle barrels on the Colonial Pipeline were pegged between 2.90 and 2.60 cents under the August NYMEX, about 0.20 cents firmer than Friday morning. End-July barrels were pegged at between 3.35 and 3.00 cents under the to the print.

Prompt No. 2 heating oil also firmed about 0.20 cents in a market that appeared seller-heavy, according to market players. Prompt barrels traded at 2.30 cents to the August heating oil futures. Low sulphur diesel changed hands at 1.90 cents under the NYMEX print, even with Friday morning.

Differentials were little changed on most products, except for a half cent weakening in prompt Chicago low sulfur diesel -- offered at 1.0 cent below August futures for delivery between July 1 and July 10.

"There were lots of sellers in a thin market. When that happens, it (diffs) can come down in big chunks," one Chicago diesel trader said, noting, however, that talk had substituted for real trading activity.
Prompt Group Three diesel, meanwhile, saw diffs hold steady at between 1.10 and 1.35 cents above July futures, players said.
Group spot unleaded gasoline was offered at 4.0 cents over the July screen, while Chicago material hovered at 0.60 cent over August NYMEX, traders said.
NYH differentials barely budged in a market that saw few active players on Friday, according to traders.
Prompt regular M2 conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 3.00 cents below July futures, stable with Thursday levels.
Offers for prompt reformualted A2 gasoline remained at 0.25 cents below the July NYMEX after edging up a tad this morning.
On the distillate side, prompt low sulfur diesel traded 0.70 cent over July NYMEX, a slightly stronger than Thursday, traders said.
